answer: Because the counters live in the echo ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. An operator running many aliases thus forfeits for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the cipher quota and the falcon admission check. Submission rate is limited to 3 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole farm from one uplink. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
